A decision agenda for the next category review

slides.speaker_notes:
1. Validate the five decisions before committing to commercial scale
Suggested speaking time: 35 seconds. Main discussion: approximately 8–9 minutes; two appendix slides support questions.

TALK TRACK
The recommendation is to validate five concrete decisions, not to approve a category-wide rollout or a financial target. Start with prerequisites—availability and listing—then settle lifecycle questions and test commercial changes with a baseline. The review is based on synthetic data, and no business benefit has yet been measured.

slides.title: Approve a focused pilot—not a category-wide rollout

elements.text: Approve a focused pilot—not a category-wide rollout
Three conclusions for leadership; one bounded decision to take today.

33 stock flags: 9 out of stock, 24 low stock.
2 in-stock products have zero-sales signals.

Check supply, listings and feeds
before promotional spend.
Reassess range decisions; do not automate them

19 inactive products have growing market proxies.
The reasons for inactivity are not supplied.

Confirm the reason for inactivity
before changing the range.
Treat modeled value as a test hypothesis

Peer benchmarks provide scenarios—not forecasts.
No realised uplift, ROI or time saving is measured.

Agree a baseline and test economics;
expand only after observed results.
Decision requested: endorse the five checks, name accountable owners and agree pilot success criteria.

slides.speaker_notes:
2. Approve a focused pilot—not a category-wide rollout
Suggested speaking time: 60 seconds. Main discussion: approximately 8–9 minutes; two appendix slides support questions.

TALK TRACK
This is the governing answer. We recommend a limited, evidence-led pilot, not a broad promotional programme or automated range change. The immediate agenda is operational validation, lifecycle context and explicit economics. Leadership should endorse the initial five checks, nominate owners and require agreed success criteria before any test or production investment. The recommendation is managerial judgment informed by the snapshot, not an observed customer mandate.

The 134 rule-matched products form a complete, mutually exclusive decomposition using each SKU's primary action: 35 operational validation, 48 range decisions, 51 commercial review / testing. They require different responses rather than one generic opportunity score. Secondary flags are not extra products. 101 products matched no rule; they have not been certified healthy. The 18 assortment cells are a separate unit of analysis.

6. Shortlist economics are much smaller than the full scenario pool
Suggested speaking time: 80 seconds. Main discussion: approximately 8–9 minutes; two appendix slides support questions.

TALK TRACK
The earlier headline totals refer to the full rule-matched queue. The selected five contain only €9,986.05 of revenue benchmark-distance scenarios across 2 cases, and €4,422.43 of gross-profit scenarios in 1 case. These must never be added, and the 2 unquantified decisions are not zero-value opportunities. The peer distances are not causal forecasts. Gross profit holds current revenue constant, not volume or net profit. Costs, elasticity and cannibalisation are not modeled, the performance-window end is unknown, and annualisation is not justified.

slides.speaker_notes:
7. A review record makes each decision owned and measurable
Suggested speaking time: 60 seconds. Main discussion: approximately 8–9 minutes; two appendix slides support questions.

TALK TRACK
This is where the prototype becomes a usable product slice rather than only an analysis. Its four-step loop keeps evidence, decision, proposed ownership and a checkpoint together. The role scorecard is a proposed management cadence, not observed adoption. We have not measured time saved or business uplift. Local storage does not make this a shared workflow tool, and accepting a plan item changes no stock, prices or assortment.

8. Scale only after validation and a controlled pilot demonstrate value
Suggested speaking time: 65 seconds. Main discussion: approximately 8–9 minutes; two appendix slides support questions.

TALK TRACK
Leadership can approve a focused validation agenda without committing to a rollout or a quantified savings claim. Gate one settles data and business context. Gate two defines the treatment, costs, baseline or control and the success threshold before testing. Gate three reviews actual outcomes and adoption before considering production tooling. Owners and gates here are proposed, not assignments or a delivery promise. If evidence does not support a test or expansion, defer or stop. No dates or budgets have been invented.

slides.speaker_notes:
9. Appendix: source controls keep the interpretation defensible
Suggested speaking time: 45 seconds. Main discussion: approximately 8–9 minutes; two appendix slides support questions.

TALK TRACK
This appendix is the method, not the main recommendation. It joins the three source types, validates data structure and applies explicit business guardrails. Ranking thresholds are transparent heuristics—not learned causal effects. The same product IDs and evidence appear in the dashboard, exports and this deck. Competitor scores outside 0–100 are excluded from popularity calculations but preserved as raw evidence. Dates, role ambiguity and product comparability constrain how far a stakeholder can act.
